Chance, now live on Starknet. AI agents are increasingly being trusted to move money. Chance prevents agents from hallucinating with your money. Before an agent transaction executes, Chance simulates the exact action and checks it against the user’s mandate. If it does not match, it is blocked before funds move. On Starknet, Chance uses programmable escrow wallets. Agents can propose transactions, but funds only leave escrow when the proposed action satisfies the user’s mandate. Additionally, Chance will use Starknet’s privacy framework, STRK20, to keep an agent’s mandate and settlement context private, while allowing receipts to be selectively disclosed when needed. This is what Starknet enables for the agent economy: agents can act, but users keep control of the rules, the funds and what stays private. Welcome, @Chance_

2026 is the year Starknet officially shifted toward revenue-generating activity. The early results are starting to show: annualized revenue is up ~1,200% YoY. 2026 is also the first year Starknet has become profitable. And that matters beyond simply having a positive bottom line: it shows the network is starting to build an economic engine that can sustain its own growth. For years, the industry has largely optimized for TVL, incentives, users, and narratives. But sustainable revenue is what turns a blockchain from infrastructure people speculate on into an economy that can sustain itself: more activity → more fees → more revenue → more resources to grow the network. Ultimately, a network needs real economic activity. And Starknet is now profitable and accelerating on the revenue side. All of this before StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation have even launched their first DeFi products. Still a long way to go, definitely. But the engine is starting to turn.
Starknet can already handle 1,000 private TPS today. It will soon reach 10,000 while being fully post-quantum secure. Just saying.
Starknet is a bet on post-quantum security. 🔭🧎‍♂️

The world is finally waking up to the quantum threat. But the STARK whitepaper discussed post-quantum security eight years ago, and Starknet was built on that foundation from day one. Now, we’re finishing the job.
